viewer.cap: The morning read. Every half hour the system goes back over your workspace on its own and writes down what it noticed, in plain sentences. You get the short version and the one thing worth doing first.
viewer.stage:
WHILE YOU WERE OUT

20d
Warby Parker has sat at proposal for three weeks with no next step.
14d
Liquid Death has gone quiet — their people team is three deep and mid-launch.
8d
The Notion pilot is eight days in and two of four recruiters have not touched it.

And one you did not ask for — every deal you have won rode a dated expansion event. None of the cold ones landed.

viewer.cap: A live call. Discovery Studio is a console you run the call from, not notes you write after it. It shows the question, what to listen for, and the moment they answer you tap what you heard — it hands you the exact next line.
viewer.stage:
PAIN & CONSEQUENCE · MAKE THE COST REAL

Walk me through what happens the week a new store opens.

Listen for whether this pain is really theirs to fix, or a polite nice-to-have — and who flinches when you name the cost.

“It is messy but we cope”
“We just hired two more recruiters”
“Not a top priority”

They hired around it. Ask what that cost, and who signed it off — you have just found your economic buyer.

viewer.cap: A deal going quiet. Future Autopsy writes the story of how a deal dies before it does — names the pattern, counts the days you have left, and routes you to the room where the fix happens.
viewer.stage:

Warby Parker dies in 20 days, and here is how.

You have one champion and no one above him. Marcus goes quiet in week two, nobody signs, and it closes as no decision — the way most of your losses have gone.

pressure before clarity
seen 4×

get a second name in the room this week

tabs.label: Outbound
tabs.panel:
WRITING TO LENA, HEAD OF PEOPLE AT CHOMPS

Lena — I saw Chomps announce two new plants.

That creates several hundred production hires on a deadline, and from the outside it appears the people team will absorb most of the load. Screening is often the first bottleneck.

Worth twenty minutes next week to compare how you are staffing the openings?

Why now
Two plants announced · limited recruiting capacity
Buyer request
20 minutes next week
Copy the message

Outbound. Select an account, contact, and recent trigger. Antaeus uses all three in the draft and blocks generic messages that could apply to any prospect.

tabs.label: Cold call
tabs.panel:
BEFORE YOU DIAL · CALL STRUCTURE

Open
Identify the problem
Confirm business impact
Request the meeting
Wrap

THEY WILL PROBABLY SAY

“We are too small for something like this.”

Small teams feel a bad hire hardest. Ask what one unsuccessful store-manager hire cost last year. Their answer gives you a concrete financial impact to discuss.

Review before you dial · log the outcome after the call

Cold call. Review the call structure, likely buyer objections, and recommended responses before you dial. Log the outcome after the call, not while speaking.

tabs.label: LinkedIn
tabs.panel:
GYMSHARK · RECOMMENDED LINKEDIN ACTION

Ask — only once it is warranted
Connect, now she knows your name
Give her something before you ask
Say something useful on her post
Watch what she posts

Poppy accepted last week. Give her something today — do not ask yet.

LinkedIn. For each account, Antaeus recommends the next relationship-building action: follow relevant posts, contribute something useful, connect after familiarity exists, and offer value before asking for time. Do not begin with a direct message.
